proposals.title: Points on the table: the report prices every miss and re-scores itself as you fix
proposals.what: Server: GET /api/session/{sid}/results adds `ledger`. (a) For each Incorrect or Unanswered question, `points` = the midpoint of section_score with that question flipped to correct on the same route, minus the actual midpoint, rounded to 10. It uses scoring.py's own weights (1/2/3) and anchors. (b) Rows grouped by (template, reason), with points summed. (c) `on_table`: the estimate with every easy and medium miss flipped. (d) `route_flip`, for lower-routed sittings: the fewest Module 1 misses, cheapest first, that reach 60%, as {k, qids, ceiling_from: 580, ceiling_to: 800}. (e) `recovered`: for each miss, the first clean attempt on the same template after the sitting (a twin, Fix these or a retake), marked recovered or relapsed. (f) `rescored`: scoring.score and section_score re-run with recovered misses counted right, as {low, high, n_substituted, as_of}. UI: the hero gauge adds a hatched orange segment from the band's high to on_table.high, labelled '+60 on the table', and a graphite tick 'Now 560–690' when rescored differs. A new block #ledger sits under the hero. Its heading reads '+60 points on the table · 9 questions'. Its rows are sorted by points, e.g. '+20 · Largest value as the bottom of the range · M1 Q1, M2 Q6 · Linear inequalities · Open', each with Review and Try one like this. The route line (lower route only) reads '1 more right in Module 1 (cheapest: M1 Q3, easy) would have sent you to the harder Module 2 and lifted the 580 cap.' A progress bar reads 'Recovered +30 of +60 since Sep 23', with a ✓ on each recovered row. The primary split pill gains 'Recover +60 · 9', which POSTs /api/drill {from_session, only: qids in points order, each: 2}. The player's bottom bar gains 'Next costliest' (key N walks misses by points, not by index). On Results, a sitting card shows 'Now 560–690' beside the original band when the two differ by 20 or more, and the score chart draws that as a hollow dot above the sitting. Every figure is labelled 'on this report's scale'.
proposals.beats: Their report stops at '420/1600' and a red grid, and says nothing about which misses matter or how many points each cost. They also cannot re-score an old report: re-answering their fixed item after seeing its key measures memory. We measure recovery on fresh twins of the same question type. It also goes far past the spec's single what-if line (easy misses only, one number).
proposals.needs: A flip helper in scoring.py (F4). Twins with cfg.parent (R24, F5). Attempts after the sitting, looked up by template. Trap state (R9). estimate.py for the chart's hollow dot (R16). A hatched segment and tick in UI.gauge (F1 charts.js).

proposals.title: Why each miss happened: Concept, Slip, Second-guess, Time or Guess, each with evidence and its own remedy
proposals.what:
Server: each review item gains `cause {kind, evidence[]}`. The first matching rule wins:
1. guess: qstate conf == guess.
2. second_guess: the trail held the key before the final answer.
3. time: answered with under 60 s left on the module clock in under 30 s, or blank among the last 3 positions reached with under 2 min left.
4. slip: easy or medium; right on this template before, or topic mastery ≥ 0.65; and ms under 60% of the student's median for that tier.
5. concept: trap hits_all_time ≥ 2, or conf == sure, or topic mastery < 0.4.
6. Otherwise unclear.
A later twin updates the label: right on the first try within a day → 'Slip · confirmed'; wrong → concept.

Report:
- A stacked bar under the tiles: '13 misses: 5 Concept · 3 Slip · 2 Second-guess · 2 Time · 1 Guess'. Each segment is a review filter.
- Every mistake row and the player header carry a cause chip with its evidence, e.g. 'Slip · easy · 0:21 (your easy median 0:58) · right on this type 3 times before'.
- 'Colour by' gains Cause.

One remedy button per cause:
- Concept → Fix these (twins, each 2).
- Slip → 'Careful set · 10': easy and medium twins of the slipped types, one attempt, 1:15 each, no retry.
- Second-guess → the answer-changes rule line plus a drill of the changed types.
- Time → 'Pace set · 10 at 1:15', plus a link to the module timeline.

The student can relabel a cause from its chip ('It was a slip'). The label is stored and sets the trap's kind, since R9 already has the kinds slip and unsure. Results adds 'Causes over the last 5 sections' as stacked bars.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep colours a miss red and stops there. Their review payload has no time, answer trail or confidence, so they cannot tell a careless miss from a knowledge gap. The spec shows pace chips and answer changes as separate facts, but never assigns a cause to a miss or a different remedy per cause.
proposals.needs: qstate ms, trail and conf, plus the module clock at each answer (`left`), from the S5 runner (R7). Per-template history and mastery (progress). Trap kinds (R9, F4). Drill body fields for per-question clock and retry off, for the careful and pace sets (F5 §2.6).

proposals.title: Paired retake: every question type compared one-to-one (Fixed / Held / Slipped / Stuck)
proposals.what:
This builds on the spec's 'Retake as a test' (mock/new {like}).

Server: mock/new {like} stores cfg.pairs {new_qid: source_qid} for each slot, with Module 2 paired only when the route matches. A retake's results add `pair {source, matrix {fixed, held, slipped, stuck}, rows[]}`.

The retake's report gets a 'Compared with Section #7' block right under the hero:
- A 2×2 matrix: Fixed ✕→✓ 7 · Held ✓→✓ 26 · Slipped ✓→✕ 3 · Stuck ✕→✕ 4. Each cell is a review filter.
- The score delta is labelled 'Same question types, new numbers'.
- If Module 2 routed differently: 'Module 1 compared (22 types); Module 2 took the other route.'

On a paired question, the player shows tabs 'Sep 30 (this) · Sep 23 (original)' at the same position, so the same trap is visible in both.

'Re-sit my misses' is a mini parallel form: twins of the missed types plus an equal number of correct types as controls, timed at 95 s each, with feedback at the end. Its report reads e.g. 'Fixed 6 of 9 · controls held 8 of 9'.

'Retake in 7 days' adds a task to the active plan on the 7th study day (POST /api/plan/{id}/tasks); with no plan, it becomes a reminder on Today.

'Compare with…' on any two sittings of the same kind (no pairs needed) shows domain, skill, cause and pace side by side.
proposals.beats: A TopTierPrep paper can only be retaken with the same items, so the second score measures memory, and their 29 papers run out. Ours never run out, and the comparison is exact per question type rather than two unrelated totals.
proposals.needs: POST /api/mock/new {like} and blueprint.draw_matching (spec, S5). cfg.pairs. A drill under test rules with end-mode feedback (F5). Plan task endpoint (S7). A two-tab mode in UI.review (F3).

proposals.title: Confirm this score: which rights were solid and which were luck, in 15 minutes
proposals.beats: Their estimate card prints 'LOW CONFIDENCE' in red and offers nothing but another full test. Ours names the rights that were luck and raises the confidence in 15 minutes. Re-testing a right answer needs a fresh item of the same type, which only a generator can supply.
proposals.needs: Confidence tags and per-question time (S5 qstate). A twin drill under test rules (F5). A confirmation input to estimate.py (F4, R16). Trap kind unsure (R9).

proposals.title: Error profile: misconception families that cut across topics, with a drill for the habit
proposals.what:
Bank: each Mis gains `family` from a closed list of about 12:
- answered the wrong quantity
- stopped a step early
- sign or direction
- inverse operation
- percent base
- squares and roots
- part vs whole
- confused pair (radius/diameter, mean/median, slope/intercept)
- units and conversion
- misread the table or graph
- counting (off by one, doubled once)
- set-up
The bank has 894 distinct distractor reasons; about 195 contain 'instead of' and many 'rather than' or 'stopped'. A script tags by keyword, a person reviews the rest, and audit asserts that every distractor has a family. attempts and traps store `family`.

Report: an 'Error profile' block after Mistakes:
- One bar per family, with its count and the topics it spans, e.g. 'Answered the wrong quantity ×4 · Ratios, Linear functions, Percentages'.
- Each bar is a review filter and has 'Drill this habit · 10'. That POSTs /api/drill {family, count}, which picks templates across topics whose options carry a distractor of that family, weighted to the student's weak topics, so the same trap is met in new settings.

Results: the family trend across the last 5 sections; the Skill panel lists each skill's families.
proposals.beats: Their 'Distractor Analysis' is prose written per item, so it cannot be counted or grouped. Ours is labelled data. We can tell a student 'your problem isn't percentages, it's answering an intermediate value', and train that habit across topics, which no finite prose bank can do.
proposals.needs: A bank change (T-bank), which is also open question 18's stable misconception tag. attempts and traps columns (F4). A `family` field in the drill body (F5). Review uses the same field (S10).

proposals.title: How you got your wrong answer: the wrong path worked with your numbers, beside the key's
proposals.what:
Bank:
- Item gains `steps`: the key's worked solution with this seed's numbers.
- Each Mis gains `work`: the steps that produce that distractor, ending in its value.
- audit checks that the last number of each `work` equals the option's value.
- Coverage starts with the 50 templates with the most trap hits and grows; the rest fall back to the reason text.

Player:
- Under the picked wrong option, 'How you got B' shows the wrong path. 'The key's path' sits beside it (stacked on phone).
- The first step where the two paths differ is marked in orange ('Here: you took 99 as the bottom').
- After a twin is answered, 'Same trap, new numbers' shows a diff built from params: '43 → 51, 99 → 88. The trap answer would now be 88 ≤ t ≤ 139.' This shows the trap is a rule, not a number.
- Hide answers hides both paths.
- Print includes the paths for misses.
proposals.beats: Their explanation is a long 'Justification' plus one generic line per distractor. Ours reproduces the student's own arithmetic from the item's parameters and points at the exact step where it went wrong. A hand-written bank needs a writer for every option of every item; our templates write it once per template, for unlimited seeds.
proposals.needs: Template changes in satbank; params already exist on all 386 templates. An audit rule. `steps` and `work` on review items, behind R19 access. Rendering in UI.workspace's review mode (F3).

proposals.title: Crowd rarity: misses that most students get right come first
proposals.what:
Server: statistics per template × tier, pooled over every seed and every learner's first clean tries (R8 filters): `crowd {pct_right, n, top_trap {label, share}, solve_ms}`. It is on each review item when n ≥ 20 and hidden below that. Letters move between seeds, so the spread is by misconception label, not by letter.

Report:
- The Mistakes sort gains 'Most students get these', which is the default. Rows show '84% of students get this type right'.
- A tile: 'Unusual misses · 4 · types 80%+ of students get right'.
- The player shows '64% of 412 students got this type right. Most common wrong answer: "largest value as the bottom" (41% of misses)', plus 'You fell for the most common trap' or 'a rare one'.
- The Details popover adds the measured level 1–7 (QBank's) and the % right.
- Pace compares with correct solvers: 'Students who get this right take 1:10; you took 2:40'.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's only crowd number is a first-attempt percentile, and their report has no statistics per question. A fixed item needs a crowd of its own; ours pool across every seed of a type, so they fill quickly and cover every question, and they are keyed to named misconceptions.
proposals.needs: The drill.levels() crowd cache (QBank, F5/S4). R8's clean-answer filters. The n ≥ 20 threshold (open question 12). UI.spread (F1).

proposals.title: Your next 50 points: a gain forecast per skill, with your own time cost
proposals.what:
Server: GET /api/forecast, plus a `forecast` field on one sitting's results. For each open trap and each weak skill:
- points per section = expected questions of that topic on a section (blueprint DOMAIN_SPLIT spread over the domain's topics) × the average weight at the student's route tiers × their current first-try miss rate, converted with the scoring slope;
- minutes to fix = the student's median attempts to close a trap, from their closed traps (default 4) × their average ms at that tier.

Report: #next becomes 'Where your next points are':
- Rows such as 'Linear inequalities · ~+20 · about 25 min for you · 2 open', sorted by points per 10 minutes, each with Start (a drill of that skill's traps) and 'Add to plan'.
- A total line: 'Fix the top 5: ~+50 in about 1 h 40 m. Target 700 needs +40.'

Results: the same list over all history, set against the exam date ('10 days · 45 min a day covers the top 7').

Every number is labelled an estimate, with a 'How this works' disclosure.
proposals.beats: Their plan copy says it weights weak areas, but it shows no numbers, and their generator failed 3 times out of 3. No TopTierPrep screen says what a skill is worth or how long it will take this student. We record each student's repair rate and time per answer, so we can compute both.
proposals.needs: Blueprint shares (S5 blueprint.py). Trap history with closes (R9). attempts.ms for tests (R7). The scoring slope in estimate.py (R16). Plan tasks (S7).

proposals.title: Where the clock went: a module timeline of visits, changes, flags and away time
proposals.what:
The runner records `visits` for each qid as [start_s, end_s] from the module start (capped at 30 per qid) in qstate, alongside the pauses and away time it already tracks.

Report: #timeline has one lane per module, with an x-axis of 0–35:00:
- each visit is a block filled with the question's final status;
- answers are dots and changes are ticks;
- flags are notches;
- away periods are hatched;
- pauses are gaps labelled 'Paused 4:10'.

Facts under the lanes:
- 'Reached Q22 with 1:10 left'
- '3 hard questions took 9:40 for 1 right'
- 'Revisited 4 of 5 flagged; changed 2, both to right'
- 'Flagged and never revisited: M2 Q19'
- 'Away from the window 2 times · 3:10'

Filter chips: 'Time sinks · 3', 'Never revisited · 1', 'Answered in the last 2 minutes · 4 (2 wrong)'. Tapping a block opens the player at that question. On a phone the lanes scroll inside their own box, never the page, and a list view is offered.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep stores no time per question (their review payload has none), and their QBank stopwatch resets on reload. Bluebook shows none either. The spec's pace bars show seconds per question, but not the order, the revisits or the rush at the end of a module.
proposals.needs: visits and made_left in qstate (S5, R7). The pause and away fields from the Tests spec. A lane chart in charts.js (F1).

proposals.title: A fresh printable paper from any report, with an online answer code
proposals.what:
The ⋯ menu gains:
- 'Print a parallel section · 44 fresh questions': the same blueprint slots and templates on new seeds, as Retake builds.
- 'Print my misses with new numbers', ×1, ×2 or ×3.

Both open /review/print.html:
- numbered stems, figures, choices and space to work;
- last pages: the answer key, each option's misconception, and the worked steps where the template has them (proposal 6).

A code and QR at the top read 'Enter your answers at …/w/K7Q2PX'. They open the same items as an end-mode set to type answers into. Those answers are marked and filed, and that set's report compares with the original sitting.

Seeds are remembered as seen, so practice never serves them again. The read-only tutor view gets the same two buttons.
proposals.beats: Their 'Share / Export Report' button does nothing. A finite bank can only print questions the student has already seen, with the key. Ours prints a new paper every time, and the printed answers can still count.
proposals.needs: /api/review/worksheet (Review, S10) extended with {session, only, each, parallel}. R19 access. A set code (R18, F6). End-mode sets (F5). Print CSS (F1).

proposals.title: Instant key check when a student reports a wrong key
proposals.beats: Their report form is a black box: a 0/5000 text field and 10 images, and no answer. Our items are verified by two independent computations, so we can answer the student on the spot and correct the score when we were wrong.
proposals.needs: R17's report dialog (F6). The satbank audit, callable for one item. R8 `disputed`. Re-scoring (proposal 1). The admin reports list (Shell).

proposals.title: Calibration: how sure you were against how right you were
proposals.what:
Report #calibration, for tests with confidence tags:
- A table of Sure / Unsure / Guess by right / wrong: 'Sure 25 · 92% right · Unsure 12 · 58% · Guess 7 · 29%'.
- The top row is 'Sure and wrong · 2', headed 'Mistakes you believe: fix these first'. It lists their misconceptions, and they move to the top of Fix these.
- Flag accuracy: 'Flagged 3, 2 of them wrong. Your doubts are worth trusting: revisit your flags.'
- 'Lucky rights · 3' (guessed and right) links to Confirm this score (proposal 4).

Results: the calibration trend across sittings ('Sure answers right: 84% → 92%').
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep has flags only, and uses them as a filter. They never record confidence, so they cannot find the misconceptions a student holds with certainty, which are the most urgent to fix.
proposals.needs: qstate conf (S5, the Tests spec's Sure/Unsure/Guess tags), which the Report spec currently never renders. Flags (R5). Trap ordering (R9).

proposals.title: Head-to-head on a shared test, and a rematch on new numbers
proposals.what:
When the sitting came from a shared test (the Tests spec's `peers`, which the Report spec never renders), a 'Friends on this test' block shows:
- each peer's band, when they allowed it;
- one ✓ ✕ – strip row per person across the questions, so 'only you missed M1 Q7' and 'everyone fell for "largest value as the bottom"' are visible.

The player shows '2 of 3 friends got this right'.

'Rematch with new numbers' creates a parallel shared test (same templates, fresh seeds) and copies its link.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's QBank share only copies a session for someone else to start, and nothing compares the results. A rematch on fresh numbers is only possible with a generator.
proposals.needs: Tests' `peers` field and sets (R18, S5). mock/new {like} (proposal 3).
